finding.claim: GET /users returns the id and name of every user in any org the caller names. The org comes from the query string, and no authentication or authorization is applied in this file. An unauthenticated caller can enumerate other tenants' users. This holds unless auth middleware outside this file sets req.pg and enforces org scoping, and none is visible here.
finding.source: req.query.org, an unauthenticated attacker-controlled query parameter
finding.sink: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1, with the result returned via res.json

trace.note: The route is registered with no auth middleware. Only app.get is used, and no app.use appears anywhere.
req.query.org goes straight into the query as the tenant filter. It is not compared with any session or user org.
The rows are returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: The SQL is parameterized ($1), so there is no injection. I found no authentication, session or org-ownership check in db.js. The only file in the directory is db.js, so any middleware would have to live elsewhere. I did not find one.

verdict.guard_found: none (the query at db.js:9 is parameterized, which stops SQL injection but is not an access control; there is no app.use, auth middleware or org check in db.js, the only file in the directory)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth middleware, passes the caller-supplied req.query.org as the tenant filter at db.js:9, and returns the rows at db.js:10, so an anonymous caller can read any org's users; the one caveat is that middleware outside this file could not be seen, and none exists in the directory.
